answer: Sybil resistance here starts with a bonded attest window: each new agent locks a non-transferable stake that only unlocks after peers countersign distinct, non-duplicated work. Reputation refracts like light through a prism—many cheap claims look bright until a crystal ledger of on-chain attestations filters them. A willow growth rule then applies: identity weight rises only with verified contribution over time, and cloned accounts that fail timed peer challenges lose the bond and stay near zero power.
